rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING SUPPORT FOR THE SURVIVING SPOUSE AND CHILDREN OF SLAIN JUSTICES AND JUDGES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 910, AS AMENDED, ENTITLED \"AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR THE RETIREMENT OF JUSTICES OF THE SUPREME COURT AND OF THE COURT OF APPEALS, FOR THE ENFORCEMENT OF THE PROVISIONS HEREOF BY THE GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM, AND TO REPEAL COMMONWEALTH ACT NUMBERED FIVE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SIX\", AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Providing Support For The Surviving Spouse And Children Of Slain Justices And Judges, Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 910, As Amended, Entitled \" An Act To Provide For The Retirement Of Justices Of The Supreme Court And Of The Court Of Appeals, For The Enforcement Of The Provisions Hereof By The Government Service Insurance System, And To Repeal Commonwealth Act Numbered Five Hundred And Thirty-six\"
rows.abstract:
Entitles the surviving spouse and children of the slain judge or justice the salary plus the highest monthly aggregate of transportation, representation and other allowances such as Personal Economic Relief Allowance (PERA) and additional compensation allowance received by an associate justice of the Supreme Court; and a gratuity equivalent to ten (10) years salary, lump sum, to be computed based on all the salaries and other benefits of an associate justice of the Supreme Court.

Provides that upon the death of the surviving spouse, the benefits of such spouse was receiving shall be transferred to the surviving children of the slain justice or judge.

Provides further, that if the surviving spouse and children have not received the full lump sum due them within one (1) year from the death of the justice or judge, the lump sum still to be granted shall be computed based on the difference between the amounts already received and the ten (10) year lump sum based on the current rates of salaries, benefits, allowances and other grants given to an associate justice of the Supreme Court.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2018-11-21, transmitted to the Senate on 2018-11-22 and received by the Senate on 2018-11-22

rows.abstract:
States that the National Food Authority shall be classified as a Government Instrumentality vested with Corporate Powers (GICP), tasked to maintain safe, adequate and continuous supply, at reasonable prices of food grains in the country.
Intends to address various challenges and concerns facing the National Food Authority such as: the reasonableness and affordability of prices of staple rice and corn; enforceability of rules and regulations governing grains business; licensing and registration of all rice and corn business

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING GOVERNMENT AGENCIES TO IMPLEMENT HEALTH IMPACT ASSESSMENTS AND TAKE OTHER ACTIONS TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENT QUALITY OF COMMUNITIES
rows.abstract:
Proposes to ensure that policies, programs, or projects of the government is consistent with improving environmental health or reducing its negative impact to the community´s health and to the environment.
Aims to implement a “Health in All Policies” approach and improve accountability of policymakers for health impacts and providing emphasis on the consequences of public policies on health systems, determinants of health, and well-being.
Defines “Health Impact Assessment” as a systematic process that uses an array of data sources and analytic methods and considers inputs from stakeholders to determine the actual or potential effects of a proposed policy, program or project on the health of a population and the distribution of those effects within the population

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE NATIONAL ECONOMIC AND DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY AS THE INDEPENDENT ECONOMIC AND PLANNING AGENCY OF THE PHILIPPINE GOVERNMENT, DEFINING ITS FUNCTIONS AND AMENDING EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 230 SERIES OF 1987, AS AMENDED, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Envisions to instill a culture of planning in the formulation and implementation of the country´s economic and development policies and emphasizes the importance of participatory planning by expanding stakeholder participation through various stages.
It seeks to institutionalize a new and truly independent department, that will implement long-term, continuing, integrated, and coordinated programs and policies for national development; and that will also enhance decentralization and strengthen the autonomy of units within the various regions of the country to accelerate the economic and social growth and development.
Enumerates the powers and functions of the NEDA, the composition and powers of its Board and the creation of inter-agency committees as follows: Development Budget Coordination Committee (DBCC); Investment Coordination Committee (ICC); Infrastructure Committee (INFRACOM); Social Development Committee (SDC); Tariff and Related Matters Committee (TRMC), Regional Development Committee (RDCOM); National Land Use Committee (NLUC); Economic Development Committee (EDC); Science, Technology and Innovation Committee (STIC); Environment and Sustainable Development Committee (ESDC); and the Governance Committee (GC).

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL STANDARDS FOR BANKING AND FINANCIAL SERVICE CHARGES AND CLIENT PROTECTION AND WELFARE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to empower depositors and other bank clientele with verified, credible information and sound metrics on banking performance and services, to enable them to make well-informed decisions on how to manage their personal and business finances.

Tasks the Bangko Sentral to develop comprehensive and detailed sets of banking and financial services standards, corresponding objective indicators, and database of metrics of objective, qualitative and quantitative ratings on financial inclusion, service quality, and service charges.

Creates the Harmonized Indices of Service Quality and Charges (HISQC) System as a transparency mechanism to enable consumers to use the standards to objectively compare, monitor, and rate banking and financial services, using computer software, electronic devices, mobile applications, and other means of telecommunications.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING A BAN ON DUMPING OF SEWAGE SLUDGE AND INDUSTRIAL WASTE INTO THE SEA
rows.abstract:
Aims to provide protection to our marine and aquatic life and resources by penalizing the act of dumping of wastes into the sea waters.

Defines “Industrial waste” as any solid, semi-solid, or liquid waste dumped by a manufacturing or processing plant; and “Sewage sludge” as any solid, semi-solid, or liquid waste generated by a wastewater treatment plant.

Penalizes any person or the guilty officer/s (in the case of corporation, trust, firm, etc.) who dumps above-mentioned wastes into ocean waters, an amount of not less than ONE HUNDRED THOUSAND PESOS (Php100,000.00) nor more than ONE MILLION PESOS (Php1,000,000.00) or imprisonment of not less than SIX (6) months but not more than EIGHT (8) years, or both at the discretion of the court.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ESTABLISH A JOB TRAINING PROGRAM FOR MATURE OR OLDER WORKERS
rows.abstract:
Defines several terms among others as follows:

Basic Skills Deficient - means with that the individual has English reading or computing skills at or below the 8th grade level on a generally accepted standardized test or a comparable score on a criterion-referenced test; Mature or Older Worker - means an individual who is 40 years of age or older.

Intends to provide programs to prepare mature or older workers for involvement in the working force, by enrolling them to occupational and educational skills that they may use for an improved skill set and long-term employability.

Enumerates several categories for an individual who shall be eligible to participate in the program and provides for program design which covers general program requirements; authorized trainings or support services, and special rules on selection of service providers and job training plan.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE COMMISSION ON ELECTIONS TO PROVIDE FIELD OFFICES FOR THE PROVINCIAL ELECTION SUPERVISOR AND ELECTION REGISTRAR, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 55 OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES\", AS AMENDED, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE IMPOSITION OF INTEREST AND/OR PENALTY CHARGES ON UNPAID HOSPITAL BILLS AND MEDICAL EXPENSES OF PATIENTS WHO EARN AN INCOME OF THE MINIMUM WAGE OR LESS
rows.abstract:
Declares it unlawful for any hospital or medical clinic to charge interest or impose other penalties on unpaid bills for ONE YEAR from the date of the discharge, to patients who earn minimum wage or less and of minor patients whose parents or legal guardians also earn minimum wage or less,

Penalizes any hospital/medical clinic officer or employee who violates the provisions of this Act by a fine of Twenty Thousand Pesos (P20,000.00) to Fifty Thousand Pesos (P50,000.00), or imprisonment of one (1) month to six (6) months, or both such fine and imprisonment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2018-09-04

rows.author: I105;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REGULATION, SUPERVISION AND PROFESSIONALIZATION OF THE PRACTICE, LICENSING AND REGISTRATION OF SANITARIANS
rows.abstract:
Aims to recognize the roles of sanitarian in our society by equipping them with the proper knowledge, training and skill-set required to effectively and properly discharge their functions.

Defines “Sanitarians and Hygiene Profession or Practice of Sanitation and Hygiene” as profession concerned primarily with education, prevention and control of diseases and other public health concerns using scientific methods and paramedical measure related to sanitation and hygiene.

Provides for the description and scope of work of sanitary inspectors as follows:
a) Waste management; b) Food and water supply sanitation; c) Vermin and vector control; d) Industrial hygiene; e) Epidemiology; f) Pollution control; g) Environmental health planning and program; h) Other community level activities re: public hygiene.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2018-09-04

rows.abstract:
Proposes to employ and train additional school-based mental health personnel, counselors, social workers and school psychologist in order to address the intellectual, emotional and developmental needs of the elementary and secondary school students. 

Provides that each public school shall have at least three (3) counselors, one (1) psychologist, one (1) social worker, and other mental health and students service providers when the need arises.

rows.abstract:
Creates the Department of Disaster Resilience that shall be the primary agency responsible for leading, organizing and managing the national effort to reduce disaster risk, prepare for and respond to disasters, recover and rehabilitate, and build forward better the after the occurrence of disasters.

Enables the government to quickly respond, prepare, implement, monitor, and evaluate disaster and climate resilience plans, programs, projects and activities.

Ensures that the government upholds the welfare of the people particularly the vulnerable sectors of the society by providing its citizens a safer, adaptive, resilient, and inclusive community.

rows.abstract:
